status: Additional research pass complete; revised Intel arithmetic independently verified.
root_judgment: The additional evidence improves the project but does not establish a compelling three-to-five-year LONG or SHORT. Intel remains the more tractable operating and capital research project, not a settled investment pick. Adopt the moderated CPU/reuse case as the current prospective estimate; preserve the prior higher-volume case as upside. Neither a 9/10 thesis nor quantified winning odds is established.
decisive_new_findings: TrendForce forecasts Intel unit share falling from 50% in 2026E to 42% in 2027F amid more than 40% market growth. Conditional 40–45% industry growth implies 17.6–21.8% Intel unit growth. Prefer 20% as the central 2027 forecast and retain 30% as upside; this analyst forecast is not a physical capacity ceiling.
AT&S identified Marvell on September 22 as the unnamed customer in its June Kulim announcement. Expansion for AMD and Marvell cannot automatically be assigned to Intel.
Ibiden’s new ¥151B addition ramps in October 2029–March 2030. Its separate EMIB-T schedule remains October 2027–March 2028. These announcements do not quantify Intel CPU allocation.

Intel’s existing factory-space investment and node-reuse strategy support better mature capital productivity. Adopt 0.80 host turnover, while acknowledging weak empirical calibration. Replacement, working capital and separate packaging investment remain funded.

Apollo’s proposed $40B lease is repayable equipment financing. It does not establish customer-funded hardware or refresh. The SpaceX model already charges capital and repayment; neither free-hardware value nor another financing charge is justified.

High capital spending is already discussed by professional publishers. A current public post-Q3 Visible Alpha SpaceX estimate set and full professional Intel long-term capital schedules were not established. Single-publisher forecasts are comparisons, not consensus.

entry_reference.provenance: Root-supplied dated intraday reference; not a closing price or independently retrieved by this calculator.

revised_Intel.assumptions: CPU unit growth of 20%, 25%, 18% and 12% in 2027–2030; ASP growth of 10%, 5%, 3% and 2%; modestly lower product and Foundry profits; sticky 2027–2028 capital spending; 0.80 mature host turnover; unchanged funded external packaging. Operating choices were selected before calculating revised values.
revised_Intel.interpretation: The 2030 value near the $58.11 reference price is a coincidental output of preselected operating changes. The $37.94 end-2026 intrinsic reference does not guarantee repricing. A credible earlier repricing could support a short, but that timing has not been established. Actual borrow and collateral terms have not been measured.

SpaceX: Retain the existing mature20 case: approximately $152.38 at end-2030 versus the dated $141.31 reference. The contract review adds no numerical valuation uplift. This does not establish a short: profitable renewals, internal use and a future customer-owned subset remain possible.
next_discriminating_analysis: Link accepted CPU volume, net ASP and retained profit to specific qualified-capacity dates. With 20% unit growth, approximately 19.17% ASP growth would match the earlier 30% units / 10% ASP revenue path. Pricing remains a live alternative.
Measure Intel investment after the current expansion: replacement, growth, working capital and funding must be separated. Average book-asset turnover does not identify marginal capital productivity.
Compare matched SpaceX customer and financier terms: hardware and refresh obligations, termination rights, service fees, fully burdened costs and renewals. A financing headline is insufficient.
AT&S’s November 5 results can clarify funding receipts and execution before the November 9 submission deadline; they may not reveal Intel-specific output.
presentation_limits: The model field external_revenue_B is a Products-plus-Other-plus-net-packaging capital denominator. Embedded external Foundry sales have not been separately reconstructed; do not present it as a fully reconciled consolidated revenue forecast.
End-2031 is approximately 5.155 years after the dated entry. End-2029 and end-2030 fall within the official three-to-five-year horizon; end-2031 is a boundary control, not an exact five-year target.
A numerical audit validates implementation, not the predictive accuracy of owned unit growth, margin, capital-productivity or discount-rate assumptions.

verification.result: PASS; no material numerical or double-counting issues. Owned economic assumptions remain uncertain.
